title: ACEF Coordinated Disclosure Block (incident_card / incident_report)
description: The single canonical coordinated_disclosure shape referenced by incident_card and incident_report (RFC-0002 §5.6; ACEF core_version 1.1.0). Modeled on ISO/IEC 29147 and 30111, CERT/CC and FIRST multi-party guidance, and the Stanford CRFM coordinated flaw disclosure proposal (arXiv 2503.16861). Closed: unknown keys are rejected unless `x-*`-namespaced (matching `^x-[a-z0-9-]+/?$`), per the §5.5 / Appendix-E-Q15 closure rule and the repo X6 vendor-namespace pattern (v1.1/manifest.schema.json:96-102); any `x-*` member is accepted, safely-ignorable, preserved on round-trip, and MUST NOT affect conformance. SCHEMA-ENFORCED conditionals (§5.6 Requiredness, structurally expressible in JSON Schema and encoded in this base shape): `status` is always required; on a `status: public` card the public subset is required (`status` always, `reporter_role` via the if/then below) and `embargo_until` MUST be absent (the if/then `not`). VALIDATOR-ENFORCED conditionals (cross-field semantics delegated to F-M3-VALIDATOR-RULES, NOT encoded here): Art. 73 deadline consistency (ACEF-084), the awareness_date->deadline clock math (§5.7 shortest-applicable-clock), and the profile-declared conditional-requiredness of a matching `regulatory_timeline[]` entry when `eu-ai-act-art73-2026` / `eu-ai-act-art55` is declared (§5.7 union-of-declared-profiles rule). `regulatory_timeline[]` is an order-insensitive array (one entry per applicable jurisdiction, §5.7 registry) and MUST be sorted ascending by the RFC-8785 canonical byte sequence of its elements before hashing and serialization (§5.10). The notification_timeline[] is a separate, order-significant top-level record field (§5.10) and is NOT part of this block.

^x-[a-z0-9-]+(/[a-z0-9-]+)*$.description: X6 vendor-extension namespace (§5.5 / Appendix E Q15). Accepts both the bare `x-<vendor>` form and the slash-qualified namespace form `x-<vendor>/<segment>(/<segment>)*` documented in the repo (e.g. x-freddy and x-freddy/voice-rubric-emission, as cited in v1.1/manifest.schema.json:95 and present in tests/conformance/golden-bundles/). Segments are lowercase [a-z0-9-]; uppercase keys, non-`x-` keys, and a bare trailing slash (x-freddy/) are rejected. Any matching `x-*` key is accepted, safely-ignorable, preserved on round-trip, and MUST NOT affect conformance; non-`x-` unknown keys are rejected by additionalProperties: false.

then.description: §5.6 public-state conditional (SCHEMA-ENFORCED): on a `status: public` card the public subset (`status` is always-required at the top level; `reporter_role` is added here) is required, and `embargo_until` MUST be absent. The Art. 73 deadline-consistency (ACEF-084) and awareness_date->deadline clock math are NOT encoded here; they remain delegated to the validator (F-M3-VALIDATOR-RULES, §5.7).

status.description: Disclosure state of the incident (§5.6). Always required.

reporter_role.description: Who reported the incident (§5.6). Reuses and extends the envelope obligation_role enum plus a neutral coordinator actor; required on a `status: public` card (§5.6 Requiredness), enforced structurally by the top-level if/then in this schema.

coordinator_ref.description: Entity ref (or typed relationships[] edge per §5.8) to a neutral coordinator actor.

safe_harbor_ref.description: Pointer to the rules-of-engagement / safe-harbor document (referenced, not embedded; §5.6). The self-reporter incentive/immunity question is Appendix E Q22.

embargo_until.description: Embargo expiry (ISO 8601). MUST be absent on a `status: public` card (§5.6 Requiredness), enforced structurally by the top-level if/then `not` in this schema.

regulatory_timeline.description: One entry per applicable jurisdiction; an incident is routinely reportable under several regimes at once, each with its own clock model (§5.7 registry). Order-insensitive: MUST be sorted ascending by the RFC-8785 canonical byte sequence of its elements before hashing and serialization (§5.10).

framework.description: Open, scheme-tagged jurisdiction id from the §5.7 clock registry, e.g. "eu-ai-act-art73", "eu-ai-act-art55", "us-circia", "cn-cac-2025", "kr-ai-basic-act".

clock_model.description: Clock model for this framework (§5.7 registry).

awareness_date.description: When the reporting party became aware (ISO 8601); start of the awareness clock.

deadline.description: Computed reporting deadline (ISO 8601). MAY be null when clock_model is `pending` or `risk_management_no_clock` (§5.7). An inconsistent stated Art. 73 deadline raises ACEF-084 (§7), enforced by the validator.

data_residency.description: China PIPL/DSL conflict with global export (§5.7, Appendix E Q18).

cross_border_restricted.description: Whether localization (e.g. PIPL/DSL) forbids global export of the report.

jurisdiction.description: The jurisdiction imposing the residency restriction.

remediation_timeline.description: Negotiated, complexity-keyed remediation timeline; not a fixed 90-day clock, because AI fixes often require retraining over weeks or months and depend on transferability across models (§5.6).

rationale.description: Why this remediation/disclosure date was negotiated.
